items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: I've had great fun playing things like Perfect Rag, Nonsense Rag, quite a few of the Tony Parenti ones. In fact one that he wrote, Crawfish Crawl

ctx.x: Oh yeah, yeah, and he would discuss how Mutt would change his whole phrasing and tone from one chorus to another. Yes, yes. And change the whole sound of the band. Yes, yes, yes. What about your own repertoire of tunes that you feature on clarinet?

Ah yes, well of course I don't like feature melodies and things, but we found out very very soon, very quickly when we went to England, we were playing sessions every night, that the brass men just couldn't keep up with it, lips would be shattered and so on, so that I'd have to do some numbers occasionally and it wasn't too bad because it gave me an opportunity to feature things that I used to play around with at home a bit. I like getting onto rags and piano rags and playing them on clarinet and trying to play…
What's strange do you use when you, you hear me, improvise?
